title: Virtual machine
summary: A virtual machine is software that emulates a complete computer system, allowing execution of operating systems or programs in isolated environments. System virtual machines provide substitutes for real hardware, enabling multiple isolated guest operating systems on one physical machine via a hypervisor that manages hardware sharing, often using hardware-assisted virtualization. Process virtual machines run as applications within a host operating system to support a single process, providing platform-independent execution environments; these are implemented via interpreters and can achieve performance comparable to compiled languages through just-in-time compilation. Emulators such as QEMU may also imitate different system architectures, permitting software designed for other CPUs to run. Memory optimization techniques like kernel same-page merging can share identical memory pages among co-located virtual machines.

mechanisms.title: System virtual machines
mechanisms.explanation: Provide a substitute for a real machine, enabling execution of entire operating systems. A hypervisor uses native execution to share and manage hardware, allowing multiple isolated environments on the same physical machine. Modern hypervisors use hardware-assisted virtualization, with CPU features providing assistance to the hypervisor.

mechanisms.title: Process virtual machines
mechanisms.explanation: Run as a normal application inside a host OS and support a single process. They provide a platform-independent programming environment that abstracts away underlying hardware or operating system details. Implemented using an interpreter, performance comparable to compiled languages can be achieved through just-in-time compilation.
